chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus, regarding
A Magian sold wine or pigs for a specified term, then he became a Muslim before the wealth became due. He (AS) said: 'For him are his dirhams.'

And he (AS) said: 'If a man becomes a Muslim and he has wine and pigs, then he dies while they are in his ownership and he has a debt, his creditor or his guardian (who is not a Muslim) sells his wine and his pigs and pays off his debt.'
And it is not for him to sell it while he is alive, nor to keep it.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a Muslim selling wine or pigs, or handling them if they die with debt?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the status of *Ahl al-Kitab* (specifically Magians) regarding *khamr* (wine) and *kanz* (pigs) as valid property (*mal*) that can be held and sold, even by Muslims, distinguishing them from impure waste. It establishes a practical legal precedent where a non-Muslim creditor or guardian may liquidate these commodities to settle debts, while the owner is prohibited from retaining them indefinitely or selling them personally, reflecting the Shia view of their economic agency. This ruling underscores the continuity of property rights upon conversion or death, ensuring debts are settled through the specific assets held.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, ‘Regarding

a Magian who sells wine or pigs to a named term, then he became a Muslim before the wealth was released. 
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For him are his Dirhams’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the man becomes a Muslim and for him was wine and pigs, then he dies, and these were in his ownership, and upon him were debts, his creditor or his guardian can sell to a non-Muslim, his wine and his pigs and fulfill his debts,
but it is not for him to sell it and he is alive, nor to keep it’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Isma’il ibn Marrar from Yunus who has said the following: “About the case of a of Zoroastrian man who sold wine or pigs for an appointed time, then became a Muslim before due time for payment, he (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He can have his dirhams.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘If one becomes a Muslim and owns wine and pigs, then dies while they are in his possession, and he owes a certain amount of debts, his creditor or guardian can sell his wine and pigs to non-Muslims to pay off his debts;
